## Profiles API & knowledge UI conventions

## REST conventions for profiles endpoints

- Identity lives in the URL: `/profiles/knowledge/{profile_name}` + `project_id` as a **query** param on every endpoint. Never put `project_id`/`profile_name` in a request body.
- Bodies only describe the resource (`file_name`, `content`, `title`, `overwrite`).
- `PUT` = upsert (create or replace); `DELETE` takes the resource name as a query param (no DELETE body).
- FastAPI dependencies: one `Depends` chain validates project + profile (404) and permissions (403); FastAPI caches them per request. Do not re-resolve settings inside each handler.
- Request models: `ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` + explicit `min_length`/`max_length` matching the tool limits (file name 500, content 200000, rule 4000 = `MAX_RULE_CHARS`).
- Storage `ValueError` → HTTP 400 with the message verbatim; do not string-sniff to build other codes.

## Profile knowledge UI

- `ProfileKnowledgePanel.vue` (rules/files tabs, budget bar, confirm modal) is mounted in `ProfileViewer.vue`; it reads `can_write` from the server and renders read-only with a lock hint otherwise.
- Rules are composed into `profile.content`, so any rule change must trigger a profile reload (panel emits `changed` → viewer emits `refresh`).

## WhatsApp / Channels board convention

All WhatsApp / external-channel work is tracked on board **Channels**, column **WhatsApp** (see `channels/whatsapp-bridge-architecture.md`).

Decisions already made (do not re-open):
- Official **WhatsApp Cloud API**, full duplex. The **Groups API is out of scope**: groups are created by the user in WhatsApp and codx-junior only stores group id/name + syncs messages.
- **Secrets live in global settings → `integrations[]`** (generic list, will also host Slack). Not env-var references, not in `.codx` project JSON, not in git.
- Identity: `CodxUser` carries a phone number (`wa_id`) and an `enabled` WhatsApp flag; a chat-level config lists which participants are synced.
- One group `Chat` ↔ one WhatsApp group/DM; mirrored messages tagged in `Message.meta_data["channel"]`.

## Kanban boards / sprints / task destinations

Kanban catalogue = `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (`{version, boards: {name: {id,title,description,type,parent_id,columns[],active,last_update}}, tags}`) and is read/written through `ChatManager.load_kanban` / `save_kanban`.

- A board name IS the storage folder (`.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/`) and is also stored in `Chat.board`; renaming must move the folder AND rewrite every task, deleting must not orphan tasks.
- A **sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`**; membership lives on the task (`Chat.sprints` holds sprint names). Deleting a sprint must clean `Chat.sprints` on tasks of other boards.
- Canonical task states come from `codx/junior/planning_manager.py` `STATUS_ORDER` — never hardcode a second list.
- Board/sprint/column CRUD lives in `codx.junior.tools.project_manager_tools` (`create_board`, `create_sprint`, `update_board`, `delete_board`, `create_column`, `delete_column`) and destination validation is shared via the public `validate_task_destination(chat_manager, board, column, sprints, status)`, used by `create_task` too. Tasks are always created through `TaskManager.create_task`.

## Identity: ids are canonical, names are labels

Every persisted element has an immutable `id` (UUID) and names/titles are only LABELS.

- Board/sprint: `board["id"]` in `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (a sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`).
- Column: `column["id"]` inside its board entry.
- Chat/task: `Chat.id` (also the file name suffix).
- Message: `Message.id`, mirrored with the legacy `doc_id` (`id` is canonical).
- References on a chat: `Chat.kanban_id` (board id), `Chat.column_id`, `Chat.sprint_ids`
  (source of truth for sprint membership; `Chat.sprints` keeps display names).
- Storage folder is NOT the name: each board/column carries an immutable `folder`
  (`Chat.board_folder` / `Chat.column_folder` cache it). Renaming must only change the
  title — never…

## Profiles API & knowledge UI conventions

## REST conventions for profiles endpoints

- Identity lives in the URL: `/profiles/knowledge/{profile_name}` + `project_id` as a **query** param on every endpoint. Never put `project_id`/`profile_name` in a request body.
- Bodies only describe the resource (`file_name`, `content`, `title`, `overwrite`).
- `PUT` = upsert (create or replace); `DELETE` takes the resource name as a query param (no DELETE body).
- FastAPI dependencies: one `Depends` chain validates project + profile (404) and permissions (403); FastAPI caches them per request. Do not re-resolve settings inside each handler.
- Request models: `ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` + explicit `min_length`/`max_length` matching the tool limits (file name 500, content 200000, rule 4000 = `MAX_RULE_CHARS`).
- Storage `ValueError` → HTTP 400 with the message verbatim; do not string-sniff to build other codes.

## Profile knowledge UI

- `ProfileKnowledgePanel.vue` (rules/files tabs, budget bar, confirm modal) is mounted in `ProfileViewer.vue`; it reads `can_write` from the server and renders read-only with a lock hint otherwise.
- Rules are composed into `profile.content`, so any rule change must trigger a profile reload (panel emits `changed` → viewer emits `refresh`).

Last shift I reported that the `effort` block added to `codx/junior/profiles/software_developer.profile` gives this actor 40 rounds. **It does not.** Turn 1 of *this* shift was still stopped with the plain-chat notice:

> ⏸ Turn paused by the effort budget — Maximum tool rounds (10) exceeded. This task ran as a **plain chat** (10 model rounds, no continuation).

So the profile edit is inert (or overridden). Everything below was verified this turn, by reading, on the exact hops the budget crosses:

### Hop chain (all confirmed present and mutually consistent)
| # | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `codx/junior/model/profile.py:55-116` | `ProfileEffortSettings` fields are **exactly** `max_iterations`, `continue_on_tool_limit`, `continuations`, `continuation_max_iterations` — the names I wrote |
| 2 | `codx/junior/model/profile.py:155-163` | `Profile.effort: Optional[ProfileEffortSettings]` exists |
| 3 | `codx/junior/profiles/profile_manager.py:470-485` | `load_profile` = `Profile(**json.loads(content))`; on `JSONDecodeError` it **logs and silently returns a default profile** (no effort) — the file is valid JSON today (14 lines, `python -m json.tool`-clean shape) |
| 4 | `profile_manager.py:441-457` | resolution = project `<codx>/profiles/<name>.profile` → bundled `_base_profile_path(name)`; `search_codx(modules=["profiles"], query="software_developer")` → **no match**, so in this tree the bundled file is the source |
| 5 | `chat_engine.py:1025-1036` | `_resolve_linked_profiles(query_mentions.profiles)` → `_resolve_effort_budget(sorted_profiles)` (returns `{}` when no profile carries `effort`) |
| 6 | `chat_engine.py:898-904` | the budget is **not applied in-process**: it is JSON-serialized into the internal header `EFFORT_HEADER` (`chat_engine.py:3282`, `:3544`) |
| 7 | `smol_agent.py:1100-1127` | `_resolve_effort_settings` reads `config["effort"]` or `headers["effort"]`; empty → `{}` |
| 8 | `smol_agent.py:1576-1605`, `effort.py:439-448` | `_resolve_base_policy(profile_names=…)` picks the tier by **names**, then `overrides` are applied on top |

### The one thing I cannot read
Step 7/8 log the answer every turn:
```
SmolAgent: effort tier=%s max_iterations=%d max_tool_calls=%d continuations=%d ... profile_overrides=%s
```
`search_codx(modules=["logs"])` → **skipped, the only log file is > 8 MB**. No shell, no grep, no log tail in the actor toolset.

### Operator action (30 s, decides everything)
```bash
grep 'SmolAgent: effort tier' <codx log> | tail -5
```
- `profile_overrides={'max_iterations': 40, ...}` → the override **reaches** the agent and is lost in `_apply_overrides` → fix belongs in `effort.py`.
- `profile_overrides={}` (or `tier=default max_iterations=10`) → it is lost **before** the header, i.e. `query_mentions.profiles` does not contain the shift's profile object, or the loaded profile has `effort=None` → fix belongs in the profile/mention resolution, not in `effort.py`.

Both branches are one-line-greppable facts; I cannot produce them from inside the run.

### Unchanged conclusion
Round caps and this falsification are the same underlying handicap: **no write-tool for big files (`76d97f04`), no shell (`e816cc41`), so no experiment can be run and no hunk landed.**

request.name: Delete the two duplicate flat tier profiles (codx-junior.profile, codx-junior-max.profile) created in shift 6
request.description:
## What happened (software_developer, shift 6, 2026-11-19)

Card `432b2f49` claimed the effort tiers had **no profile file**. I acted on that premise and created two flat files:

- `codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior.profile`
- `codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior-max.profile`

The premise was **false**. Both tiers already exist in folder form and were already tracked in git:

- `codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior/codx-junior.profile` (64 lines)
- `codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior-max/codx-junior-max.profile` (60 lines, `effort.max_iterations: 24`, `validation: "full+coverage+security"`)

## Why this is not currently breaking anything (but must still be removed)

`ProfileManager.base_profiles()` uses `rglob("**/*.profile")` and `list_all_profiles()` keeps the **first** profile per name (`profile_manager.py:404-407`), so duplicate names can shadow each other depending on rglob order. `_base_profile_path()` prefers the folder form `<name>/<name>.profile` before `<name>.profile` (`:181-186`), which is why the runtime still resolves the real profiles.

**Mitigation already applied in shift 6:** both flat files were rewritten as *verbatim copies* (1503 B and 1566 B) of the folder-form profiles, so whichever file wins the dedupe, the loaded profile is identical. The regression is neutralised but the files are still noise in the tree and would rot out of sync on the next edit of the folder form.

## What to do

1. `git rm codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior.profile codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior-max.profile`
2. Re-run `effort_for(["codx-junior"])` / `effort_for(["codx-junior-max"])` (or read `GET /api/profiles`) and confirm both still resolve **and** now point at the folder-form files.
3. Confirm `profile_changes` shows only `software_developer.profile` changed under `codx/junior/profiles/`.

## Acceptance

`git status` under `codx/junior/profiles/` shows no untracked flat duplicate, and both tier names still resolve to a profile whose `effort.max_iterations` is 24 (max) / agile defaults.

## Note

This needs a shell (or a delete primitive). Actor `software_developer` has `project_read_file`, `project_write_file`, `apply_file_changes` — none of which can delete a file — so this is blocked on `e816cc41` (command-execution tool) unless a human runs the two `git rm` lines.
